observed_vs_expected: The observed metrics align with the pre-declared expectations. Valid candidates (9) were generated, consistent with the hypothesis that fewer constraints improve feasibility. The tightest_margin (0.3828) confirms designs remain safely within physical bounds, and best_target_score (0.5058) did not collapse below acceptable thresholds, validating that reduced complexity successfully supported stable optimization in this single pass. No directional deviation from expected behavior is detected.
deviation_mechanism: While no unexpected deviation occurred, the objective value (0.5058) and margin (0.3828) reflect the physical limitation of initiating a 10-layer stack from a uniform 200.0 nm seed. Optical interference in the 300-450 nm band requires precise quarter-wave phase accumulation at each interface. A single heuristic pass cannot fully resolve mismatched acoustic impedances at both the air-film and film-substrate boundaries, leaving residual scattering error in the objective function and capping the safety margin until layer-by-layer phase correction converges.
continue_rationale: Only 1 round has been executed. A single initialization-to-convergence cycle cannot exhaust the multi-dimensional design space. The generation of 9 valid candidates with a robust margin (0.3828) establishes a viable baseline, but continued rounds are required to escape local minima, test alternative thickness seeds, and verify whether the reduced complexity route ultimately yields tighter margins or lower scores than baseline architectures.

Run a focused, high-resolution local optimizer on only the first and last three layers to refine boundary reflection coefficients while maintaining the established optical cavity thickness.
